chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The ghurrah (blood money for a fetus) is valued at eight dinars, and it is valued at ten dinars?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is fifty.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A title for Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْغُرَّةَ: Ghurrah: Blood money paid for the death of a fetus
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: Dinars: Gold coins used as a unit of currency in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the value of ghurrah for a fetus in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the standard valuation of the *ghurrah* (blood money for a fetus) at fifty dinars, resolving discrepancies in earlier reports. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it sets a fixed monetary benchmark for fetal compensation, distinguishing it from the variable *diyah* of a free adult. The clarification underscores the precision with which the Imams refined legal precedents to ensure consistency in financial liabilities.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The commencement (of the foetus) happens with eight Dinars, and happens with ten Dinars?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By fifty’.
